dataset_family: Singapore community MCI sample (Mind Science Centre, National University of Singapore): pooled baseline data of two NUS studies with identical assessment and MRI protocols (Klainin-Yobas et al. 2019; Lee et al. 2019 CHI study), recruited from the same community; 91 MCI with usable MRI of 121; not a public dataset
method_family: Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM): resting-state fMRI functional connectivity plus diffusion (global tractography) structural connectivity edges selected by correlation with continuous GDS-15 inside leave-one-out cross-validation, accuracy as Spearman rho(predicted, observed), significance by 10,000-fold permutation; cross-sectional, within MCI only
what_it_shows: In 91 community-recruited MCI participants (mean GDS-15 2.8, SD 3.0; 21 above the 4/5 cut-off), continuous GDS-15 depression severity was predicted out-of-sample from brain connectivity: every single-edge-type FC model and the best combined FC+SC model (rho 0.497, p < 0.001) were significant. So in this study a continuous depression-severity score DOES track structural and functional brain measures in MCI. There is no non-MCI group (the first clause is not tested) and no conversion outcome.
why: Yu et al., Prog Neuropsychopharmacol Biol Psychiatry 110 (2021) 110329. The PDF title and authors match the summaries.md block and the map entry. As a SUPPORTER of the Table A1 row the paper fails: the row's supporter sentence says 'within the supporting studies, continuous severity scores fail to track brain measures or conversion', and P-727's own analysis finds the opposite (continuous GDS-15 predicted from FC and SC under LOOCV, rho 0.497, permutation p < 0.001; positive FC edges alone rho 0.331, p 0.002). Admitting it would make that sentence false. It is counter-evidence for the brain limb, of the kind the row places outside the supporter list (as it does P-26 for the conversion limb); the current row names no brain-limb counter-study, which is a wording matter for the operator, not a reason to count this paper as support. It tests neither the first clause (all participants have MCI) nor conversion, nor the major-versus-subthreshold 'although' clause. Rejection ground answered: P-727 was removed in the bulk 2026-08-11 revert (54 -> 10) among papers described as not measuring depression; the source shows that description was wrong for this paper (it measures GDS-15 severity against connectivity), but the outcome of the rejection stands, because what it measures points against the supporter sentence, not for it. Limits that weaken the counter-evidence: the feature-selection p-thresholds were tuned by repeating the whole CPM 500 times and keeping the thresholds that gave the highest rho, and the paper does not say the tuning was repeated inside the permutations, so rho 0.497 is probably optimistic (the untuned-looking single-edge-type models are also significant, so the direction does not rest on the tuning alone); cross-sectional; symptom levels low (community sample); correlational prediction, not a group contrast; no external validation. Independence: Singapore sample, no overlap in sample, site or authors with P-643 (Korea University Guro), P-647 (Shanghai Brain Health Cohort), P-788 (Zaragoza), P-974 (Chosun) or any round-1 candidate. Not a preprint. Symbols in quotes are transliterated to ASCII (rho for the Greek letter).

quotes.quote: While FC or SC features alone significantly predicted either type of symptoms, these symptoms were best predicted by models that consisted of both FC and SC features (depression: rho predicted-observed = 0.497; anxiety: rho predicted-observed = 0.455).
The 15-item version (Sheikh and Yesavage, 1986) of the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) was used to index the level of depressive symptoms.
The inclusion criteria were 1) aged between 60 and 85 (inclusive), 2) met the criteria for mild cognitive impairment (MCI)

The remaining 91 subjects (69 females) were entered into the analyses. [...] Their mean GDS and GAI scores were 2.8 (SD = 3.0) and 2.6 (SD = 4.4), respectively. Among them, 21 and nine participants exceeded the cutoff scores for GDS and GAI
During the feature selection process in every LOOCV iteration, correlation analyses were carried out between GDS/GAI scores and all edges in the FC and SC connectivity matrices.

these thresholds were determined by repeating the entire CPM process 500 times using p-values ranging from 0.05 to 0.0001, with an interval of 0.0001 each time. Four different thresholds that produced the highest rho predicted-observed values for their respective group of features (positive SC, negative SC, positive FC, and negative FC) were selected and used subsequently in the main analyses.

First, participants were recruited from the community, consequently, their levels of symptoms, especially for anxiety, were low in general. Secondly, these participants were diagnosed with MCI. Hence it is unclear how well these findings generalize to those clinically diagnosed with depression and anxiety, as well as those who are cognitively normal.
